validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: confirmed independently. TC Energy's current operations page names 'Columbia Gas Transmission' as an active 11,899-mile (18,768 km) interstate system delivering gas across 10 states from New York to the Midwest/Southeast (https://www.tcenergy.com/operations/natural-gas/columbia-gas-transmission/, fetched live 2026-09-08). A 2023 AP wire story (Virginian-Pilot) independently confirms an active, in-service 'Columbia Gas Transmission Pipeline' along I-81 near Strasburg, Shenandoah County, VA, that TC Energy responded to after a pressure drop caused a fire — this names the pipeline and confirms present-day operation from a non-operator source. USA Today (2016) and the Columbus Dispatch/other coverage independently confirm TransCanada's $13B acquisition of Columbia Pipeline Group (parent) in 2016, consistent with today's TC Energy branding. CLASSIFICATION: correct as a SYSTEM/NETWORK aggregate row (per orchestrator scope note) rather than a segment — a system-wide figure is the right kind of ref here, unlike a segment row. DUPLICATE: checked against the 46-row roster; P2516 'Columbia Gas Transmission — Central Virginia Connector' (len=0) is a distinct discrete project, not an overlap with this network row; no other roster row plausibly duplicates this network. CITATION-POOL NOTE: two of the wiki page's own harvested references are NOT actually about this entity and should not be treated as support for P0169 — 'Northern Loop Pipeline Project' (columbiagasohio.com) belongs to Columbia Gas OF OHIO, a NiSource-owned local distribution company, not Columbia Gas Transmission LLC (TC Energy's interstate system); and the 1012industryreport.com 'Louisiana XPress' article is about Columbia GULF Transmission's Sabine Pass project, a sibling but separate TC Energy subsidiary. Both were read in full and confirmed off-topic for this row. Of the 13 harvested citations for P0169, all 13 were opened/attempted: 1 resolved via bit.ly to the Wikipedia stub (thin, no length/capacity/date data); 1 (pdigm.com PDF) is dead (404); 1 (Ohio PUC dis.puc.state.oh.us DocumentRecord) is WAF-blocked ('Request Rejected', not a confirmed 404 — access failure, not a deletion); 1 (Reuters) is paywalled (401 via curl); 1 (LNG Global) is dead (404); 1 (transcanada.com CGT page) now redirects to a generic /vendors page, i.e. retired; 1 (Columbus Dispatch) redirect-looped and was not resolved; the remaining were opened successfully as detailed above.

validity.recommendation: update LengthKnown to 18768.00 (km) per TC Energy's current operator page, or at minimum flag the value as stale
validity.researcher_notes: GEM currently records LengthKnown=19312.00 km. I found the EXACT origin of this number: TransCanada's own Columbia Gas Transmission page, archived by the Wayback Machine on 2018-12-13, states verbatim '12,000 mile (19,312 km) pipeline network' AND 'Transports an average of three billion cubic feet of natural gas per day' (= 3,000 MMcf/d, matching GEM's Capacity value exactly too). So the sheet's existing Length AND Capacity values are real, accurately-sourced 2018-vintage TransCanada figures — not fabricated. However, TC Energy's CURRENT live operator page (fetched 2026-09-08) states the network is now '11,899 miles (18,768 km)' — a ~2.9% reduction (101 mi / 544 km) from the 2018 figure, and no longer restates the 3 Bcf/d capacity figure at all. This is a material, sourced disagreement between the current authoritative primary source and the sheet's current value, so I am not silently passing it. Only one origin (TC Energy/TransCanada, at two points in time) is speaking to the exact figure — I searched for an independent second source (EIA pipeline pages: root 403-blocked to scripted clients; FERC Form No. 2 annual system-mileage filing: a full docket search was out of scope for a single-row pass; Wikipedia stub: no length stated) but did not find one, so tier is medium rather than high despite the strong single-source evidence.

validity.recommendation: re-verify StartYear1=1996 against a FERC Form 2 filing or a documented company history; I could not corroborate it and general history suggests the underlying Appalachian system predates 1996 by decades
validity.researcher_notes: GEM records StartYear1=1996 for this network row with no ref. I could not find any source — TC Energy's current page, the 2018 Wayback-archived TransCanada page, the Wikipedia stub, USA Today's 2016 acquisition coverage — that states or corroborates 1996 as an in-service/start year for Columbia Gas Transmission. Columbia Gas Transmission's predecessor entities (part of the historic Columbia Gas System) operated Appalachian transmission pipe many decades before 1996; 1996 more plausibly corresponds to Columbia Gas System's emergence from Chapter 11 bankruptcy (filed 1991) around the mid-1990s, i.e. a corporate-reorganization date rather than a pipeline in-service date — but I do not have a verified citable source for that either, so I am not proposing a replacement value, only flagging the existing one as unconfirmed. A FERC Form 2 filing or a dedicated company-history page (attempted a tcenergy.com/about/history/ guess — 404) would be the next step.
